parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
Length, mass and temperature are all SI base quantities.
State two other SI base quantities.
parts.question_text_latex:
Length, mass and temperature are all SI base quantities.
State two other SI base quantities.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The acceleration of free fall g may be determined from an oscillating pendulum using the
equation
g =(4π ^{2}l)/(T ^{2})
where l is the length of the pendulum and T is the period of oscillation.
In an experiment, the measured values for an oscillating pendulum are
l = 1.50 m ± 2%
and
T = 2.48 s ± 3%.
parts.question_text_latex:
The acceleration of free fall g may be determined from an oscillating pendulum using the
equation
$g =\frac{4\pi ^{2}l}{T ^{2}}$
where l is the length of the pendulum and T is the period of oscillation.
In an experiment, the measured values for an oscillating pendulum are
$l = 1.50 m \pm 2%$
and
$T = 2.48 s \pm 3%.$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the acceleration of free fall g.
g = m s^{-2}
